theorems.name: Cycle-033 record refinement implies no-erasure recoverability
theorems.claim: row(A_coarse) subseteq row(A_fine) implies A_coarse=P A_fine for some linear P.

theorems.name: Canonical direction of nested resource quotients
theorems.claim: N_fine subseteq N_coarse canonically induces the surjection V/N_fine -> V/N_coarse.

theorems.name: Quotient-only canonical reverse embedding
theorems.claim: Nested quotient data alone canonically determine a reverse section V/N_coarse -> V/N_fine.
theorems.smallest_counterexample: V=R^2, q(x,y)=x; sections s_a(t)=(t,a t) are moved transitively by quotient-preserving shears T_b(x,y)=(x,y+b x).

theorems.name: Fixed-metric orthogonal refinement split
theorems.claim: With one fixed positive-definite inner product, minimum-norm representatives yield Q_fine = i(Q_coarse) orthogonal-direct-sum (N_coarse intersect N_fine^perp), and dim Q_fine=dim Q_coarse+dim N_coarse-dim N_fine.

theorems.name: PDT-native metric transport across resource windows
theorems.claim: PDT primitives independently fix one shared metric or a compatible transport law across resource refinement.

theorems.name: Same-input PDT-vs-QM quantitative departure
theorems.claim: P_PDT(O|I,R) differs from P_QM(O|I,R) for identical microscopic inputs and declared resource window.
